Objective
Learn to solve isosceles triangle angle and side problems.
Definition
An isosceles triangle has at least two equal sides.
Legs
The two equal sides are called the legs.
Base
The remaining side is called the base.
Vertex
The angle between equal legs is the vertex angle.
Base angles
The angles at the ends of the base are the base angles.
Theorem
Equal sides have equal opposite angles.
Angle sum
All interior angles of a triangle total one hundred eighty degrees.
Vertex rule
Vertex angle equals one hundred eighty minus twice a base angle.
Example one
Two base angles of forty eight degrees give a vertex of eighty four.
Base rule
Each base angle equals one hundred eighty minus the vertex, divided by two.
Example two
A vertex of ninety six degrees gives two base angles of forty two degrees.
Algebra
Vertex three x plus eighteen and base x plus twenty one give an angle sum equation.
Solve
Five x plus sixty equals one hundred eighty, so x equals twenty four.
Check
The resulting angles are ninety, forty five, and forty five degrees.
Side equations
Set equal leg expressions equal to solve for x.
Perimeter
Add both equal legs and the base.
Exterior angles
Exterior and adjacent interior angles total one hundred eighty degrees.
Converse
Equal base angles imply equal opposite sides.
Triangle inequality
Any two side lengths must sum to more than the third.
Practice
